Meanwhile, our ever-expanding range of handmade grooming products continues to be THE choice of barbers across the UK and beyond. View our short film (below) shot at our flagship shop in Derby to get a flavour of our style and ethos. Better still, come along and meet the team at either of our three East Midlands barber shops. Our Story At the age of just 10 years old, Shane O'Shaughnessy began his barber apprenticeship under his beloved grandad, David Keithley (top left). No matter how gruelling his day on the docks, David provided evening barbering services for his co-orkers, friends & family and made time to mix up his own recipe hair treatments and oils to keep it affordable - with young Shane watching keenly on. By just 13 years of age, Shane too was cutting hair. After a successful career in the IT world, Shane, at the age of 36, decided to go back to his boyhood roots, and rekindle his love affair with hair. After a highly successful back-to-school style apprenticeship, Shane set up and ran a mixed salon on Peel Street in Derby, then several years later, took over a small well-established barbershop on Nuns Street in 2007 - working with friend and renowned local barber Craig Evans. Shane and Craig developed an infectious chemistry, which in turn created the perfect ambience, it seemed, for gents seeking a traditional barbershop experience. Bookings increased as the duo's reputation grew and business was booming. In 2011 Shane's thoughts turned to the hair tonics and oils his grandad used to blend, and he and his wife Sherri dusted down his old apothecary notebook and set about another ambitious project. After a year or so of developmental work, in 2012 Shane & Sherri launched The Dandy Gent - a brand new range of high-end grooming products. The products were immediately lauded by professionals and customers - the branding giving it the edge over much of the competition. Shane soon decided to rebrand his Nuns Street shop inline with the products - and The Dandy Gent Traditional Barbershop was born. Today, Shane has two shops in Derby - his original Nuns Street branch and his flagship shop in the Cathedral Quarter of Derby City Centre on Irongate. The third shop - based in neighbouring city, Nottingham - has recently outgrown its first location and in January 2022 moved to the highly desirable part of the city - Hockley. pages.https://thedandygent.co.uk/beard-balm-or: Free Delivery on all UK orders over £25 01332 265722 info@thedandygent.co.uk Book An Appointment About Us Find Us Contact Us Product User Guides More GBP £0.00 My Cart - 0 Item(s) Discounts: -£0.00 Tax: £0.00 Delivery: £0.00 Total: £0.00 View Cart Checkout Shop Book Services Digital Gift Cards The Dandy Journal Beard balm or oil Choosing between beard balm or oil is one of the first decisions any bearded gent faces. The Dandy Gent crafts premium handmade beard oils and conditioning products in Derby, blending traditional barbershop know‑how with UK‑sourced ingredients. This guide explains the difference between beard balm and oil, when to use each, and how to build a routine that keeps your beard soft, comfortable and impeccably styled. When you are ready, explore our full beard balm and oil range online or visit one of our East Midlands barbershops. Beard balm or oil – what is the real difference? Beard oil and beard balm share a common goal: to condition facial hair and care for the skin beneath. The difference lies in texture, hold and how they sit in your daily routine. Beard oil – a lightweight blend of carrier oils and fragrance. Ideal for daily nourishment, softness and healthy-looking shine. Beard balm / conditioners – richer conditioning formulas, often including ingredients such as beeswax for light hold and extra control. At The Dandy Gent, beard oils are handmade in small batches using premium UK-sourced grapeseed and pure jojoba oil, then finished with barbershop-inspired fragrances such as Rose & Tobacco, Sandalwood and Lime & Patchouli. Our beard conditioners provide additional body and light styling while maintaining that same focus on comfort and care. When to choose beard oil Opt for beard oil if your main concerns are dryness, irritation or a coarse, wiry feel. A beard oil for men is particularly useful when: Your beard feels rough, tangled or dull The skin underneath is tight, flaky or itchy You want fragrance and softness without visible product You prefer a quick morning routine that absorbs cleanly A few drops massaged from skin to tips leave the beard supple and lightly sheened – never greasy when used correctly. For guidance on matching texture and scent to your beard type, The Dandy Gent’s barbers share detailed advice in the journal article on good beard oils. When to choose beard balm or conditioner Choose balm-style conditioning products when you need both moisture and a measure of control. A quality beard balm or conditioning formula is ideal if: Your beard has medium to longer length and tends to splay or frizz You want to tame flyaways and add gentle shape You prefer a slightly fuller, more structured finish You like a subtle, natural-looking hold without stiffness The Dandy Gent’s beard conditioners and light styling products are crafted to complement our oils. Many draw on traditional barbershop formulations and may contain beeswax, offering structure while still respecting the natural feel of the beard. Using beard balm and oil together The choice is not always beard balm or oil – many clients achieve the best results by layering. Cleanse – Wash the beard with a gentle bar shampoo or cleanser to remove product and daily build‑up. Condition with oil – Apply a few drops of beard oil to damp or dry hair, working down to the skin. Finish with balm/conditioner – Work a small amount of balm or conditioner through the outer beard to add structure and control. This simple combination keeps the skin comfortable and the beard disciplined, particularly useful for those growing out shorter stubble into a fuller style. If itch is your main frustration, the Dandy Journal’s guide on how to stop beard itch offers a step‑by‑step routine built around washing, oiling and trimming. Building a complete beard care kit Whether you favour beard oil, balm or both, the right tools make a marked difference. Book your appointment online via the Nearcut app or website, or call your nearest shop in Derby or Nottingham to secure a chair. Low, mid and high fades – what’s the difference? A fade is all about a clean, gradual transition from very short hair at the sides and back into longer hair on top. The height of that transition creates the distinct looks you see every day: Low fade haircut – the fade starts just above the ear and nape, giving a subtle, refined finish that pairs well with smart or professional styles. Mid fade haircut – the blend begins roughly at the temple area, offering a stronger contrast that still remains versatile. High fade haircut – the fade sits higher up the head for a striking, contemporary look with maximum contrast between the sides and the top. At The Dandy Gent, your barber will talk you through these options at the chair, showing how each can be tailored to your head shape, hair texture and preferred styling routine. What to expect from your fade appointment The Dandy Gent operates as a traditional barbershop while embracing modern techniques, so your fade service is both classic and bang up to date. 1. Consultation and style discussion Your appointment begins with a short consultation.
